text:
Predicates:
Cute(x) ::: x is a cute animal.
SpottedNearCampus(x) ::: x can be spotted near the campus.
Turtle(x) ::: x is a turtle.
Skittish(x) ::: x is skittish.
Calm(x) ::: x is calm.
Rockie ::: Rockie.
Premises:
∀x (SpottedNearCampus(x) ∧ Rabbit(x) → Cute(x)) ::: All rabbits spotted near the campus are cute.
∃x (Turtle(x) ∧ SpottedNearCampus(x)) ::: Some turtles can be spotted near the campus.
∀x (SpottedNearCampus(x) → (Rabbit(x) ∨ Squirrel(x))) ::: The only animals spotted near the campus are rabbits and squirrels.
∀x (Skittish(x) → ¬Calm(x)) ::: If something is skittish, then it is not calm.
∀x (SpottedNearCampus(x) ∧ Squirrel(x) → Skittish(x)) ::: All squirrels spotted near the campus are skittish.
SpottedNearCampus(Rockie) ∧ Calm(Rockie) ::: Rockie can be spotted near the campus, and it is calm.
Conclusion:
(Cute(Rockie) ∧ Calm(Rockie)) → (Skittish(Rockie) ∧ Turtle(Rockie))
